content.thinking:
I need to write this postmortem without restating or inventing cost figures — the instructions are clear that impact numbers should come from what the shop actually measured, not from my own calculation. I can still reference factual details like the onset time, since that's not a fabricated figure but an observed fact.

The root cause seems to be that the account page synchronously calls the third-party payment provider's card lookup API, which began returning 503s at 15:55Z with no accompanying deploy or config change on our side — so every account page request would fail. I should flag this as inferred from logs, not confirmed with the vendor, and keep the executive summary generic by referring to "the online shop's account page" and "an outside payment company" rather than naming components directly. I also need to note key assumptions: that the 503s are causal rather than symptomatic, that the outage duration is a lower bound since metrics showed it still failing at cutoff, that automated remediation had no lever against a third-party outage, and that the proposed fix is still an unmerged draft. And I must be careful not to conflate Argus hold time with actual outage duration.

assumptions: The payment provider's 503 responses are treated as the cause rather than a symptom of something shared (e.g. a network path or DNS problem between us and them). This was inferred from our own logs and metrics; no confirmation was obtained from IO Payments Ltd, and no independent probe of their API was run.

The outage is assumed to have continued past the end of the metrics window because the service had not recovered by the last minute read. The true end time, and therefore the true duration and impact, are unknown.

The conclusion that no deploy, config, or feature-flag change contributed rests on the change and flag sources the investigator could query returning zero results. If a change was made through a path not covered by those sources, it would not have been seen.

Impact is assumed to be confined to the account page and any flow that renders card details, because that is where the failing call lives. No per-endpoint breakdown was examined to confirm the rest of the shop was healthy.
The proposed fix (pull request #58) is a draft that was neither reviewed, merged, nor verified during the incident. It is not established that it would have mitigated the failure.
Argus held the incident only briefly before escalating; that interval describes how quickly it handed off, not how long the service was broken.
input.executive_summary: Starting mid-afternoon (15:55 UTC on 27 September 2026), shoppers trying to open their account page on the online shop were met with errors. The cause was outside the shop: an external payment company's service stopped answering requests for saved card details, and because the account page waits for that answer before it can be drawn, the page failed for nearly everyone who tried to load it. Other parts of the shop that do not need card details were not implicated. Automated monitoring raised the alert within minutes and an automated responder investigated, but the failure was in a supplier's system, so there was no switch it could throw to fix it; it opened a draft code change (pull request #58) proposing that the account page tolerate the payment lookup failing, and handed the incident to people. As of the last data available, the account page was still failing, so the outage ran at least from onset to that point and possibly longer; the impact figures quoted in this report are therefore floors, not final totals. Nothing in the record shows the supplier being contacted or the page being restored.
input.root_cause: io-shop's account page makes a synchronous call to the third-party payment provider at api.io-pay.example to fetch the shopper's card while rendering the page; that provider began returning HTTP 503 for card lookups at 15:55Z, and because the call is on the critical render path with no timeout-and-degrade or fallback, essentially every account page request failed with PaymentProviderFailed (logged at src/io_shop/payment_provider.py:96). No deploy, config change, or feature-flag change was found on io-shop in the preceding window, and CPU/memory were unremarkable, which rules out an internal code or resource cause; latency rose in lockstep with errors, consistent with requests waiting on the failing downstream call before erroring.
